subject: Re: Request for temporary payment relief and staggered invoicing
messages:
From: Lidia Ramos <lidia.ramos@acme-enterprises.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: accounts-payable@acme-enterprises.com
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Request for temporary payment relief and staggered invoicing

Hi Neha,

Quick note from our finance team — Q3 cash timing is tighter than expected due to a delayed receivable, and our AP team asked whether Redwood can extend temporary terms while we sort the backlog. Specific asks:
- A one-off shift from Net30 to Net60 for the next two invoices (July and August)
- A short-term credit limit increase from $75k to $150k during that period
- If possible, split invoices into a mid-month and end-of-month run so our internal approvals can align with two funding cycles

We value the product and want to avoid interrupting usage. Happy to sign a short amendment if you need it. Also, note that some of our purchases will be VAT-recoverable through our EU subsidiary — we can provide VAT IDs if that affects invoice formatting.

Can you let me know if Redwood can accommodate this and what information you need from our side?

Thanks,
Lidia Ramos
Head of Procurement — Acme Enterprises
[Attachment: PO_Q3_pending.pdf]

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Lidia Ramos <lidia.ramos@acme-enterprises.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request for temporary payment relief and staggered invoicing

Hi Lidia — thanks for the heads-up and context. We can be flexible, but want to lock in guardrails for cash and credit exposure so both sides are protected. Proposed short-term arrangement:

1) Temporary terms: Net45 for the July invoice and Net60 for the August invoice; revert to Net30 after September.
2) Credit cap: increase to $125,000 (conditional) for 60 days. We can consider the full $150k if trade refs and the PO clear.
3) Invoice cadence: split-run option — we issue a partial invoice on the 15th (up to 50% of expected monthly usage) and a final run on the last business day. That helps you align approvals and reduces single-invoice spikes.
4) Tax/VAT: please send the VAT ID for EU-funded lines if invoicing needs EU VAT treatment. Our billing system will produce VAT-inclusive or VAT-exempt invoices as required.
5) Required items to enable: signed short amendment (we've drafted one), a PO referencing DEAL-8734, and a confirmation of ACH remit or P-card details for August.

I've attached a draft invoice run schedule (Acme_Invoice_Run_Schedule.xlsx) and the Temporary Credit Amendment draft for your legal/finance review. Marcus and Monica are cc'd to handle the credit check and final signoff.

If this is acceptable, Lidia, reply with the VAT ID (if applicable) and the PO number and we will route the amendment for signature. Plan: once signed, the first split invoice for July 15th will reflect the partial-period charge.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142
[Attachment: Acme_Invoice_Run_Schedule.xlsx]

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Lidia Ramos <lidia.ramos@acme-enterprises.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request for temporary payment relief and staggered invoicing

Thanks, Neha / Lidia — quick operational note from finance. We're comfortable with a conditional $125k uplift for 60 days once we receive:
- The PO that references DEAL-8734 and the amendment
- One trade reference (bank reference or vendor reference) or two months of historical payment behavior
- Confirmation of billing entity (US entity vs EU subsidiary) + VAT ID if EU invoicing is needed

If the above are provided within 72 hours, we can set the temporary cap and enable the split invoice run for July 15 / July 31.

Attached is a short credit checklist we ran against public data — nothing alarming but we want the documentary items captured in the amendment. If paperwork is delayed, the fallback is: Net30 + deposit equal to 30% of estimated monthly spend, to be applied to invoices.

I'll also note for the team: this arrangement should be treated as a one-time, non-precedent concession tied to the current SOW. We'll log it on the account record and require renewal discussion if similar requests recur.

- Marcus Lin
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Credit_Risk_Check.pdf]

From: Lidia Ramos <lidia.ramos@acme-enterprises.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, accounts-payable@acme-enterprises.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request for temporary payment relief and staggered invoicing

Neha / Marcus / Monica — appreciate the quick turnaround. We can accept the conditional $125k cap and the Net45/Net60 window as proposed. Next steps from our side:
- PO 2247-ACME-DEAL8734 (attached) will be uploaded to your portal by EOD today.
- VAT: our EU VAT ID for the specific BU is EU123456789 (only relevant for the 20% of spend routed through EU); please flag line items that need VAT treatment.
- We will sign the amendment via DocuSign (please send the link) — legal has reviewed and requested a 90-day review clause which we've left as a comment in the DocuSign flow.

On the split invoices: please cap the mid-month invoice at 50% of our expected monthly spend. We'll route both to accounts-payable@acme-enterprises.com. For ACH, AP will keep the same remit; P-card is not preferred.

Once the amendment is signed and PO is in, can you confirm the 15 July split invoice will be generated and that the temporary cap will be active immediately?

Thanks,
Lidia Ramos
Head of Procurement — Acme Enterprises
[Attachment: PO_2247-ACME-DEAL8734.pdf]
